value.body: Learning facilitators work with children, often in small groups, to build reading, writing and numeracy, usually through NGO, after-school or community programmes. Education NGOs, foundations and school-support programmes hire them. A day involves running activity-based sessions, assessing children and keeping records.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: D.El.Ed, or a graduate degree with an interest in teaching

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Activity-based teaching materials, assessment sheets, mobile data apps

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Facilitators are usually hired directly by NGOs for a district or project, often from the local area. Fluency in the local language and comfort working with first-generation learners matter more than formal grades.

value.title: At a glance
items: Roles are often tied to project funding and can be fixed-term.
Next steps: cluster coordinator, trainer, or programme roles.
Experience here is relevant for later school teaching posts.
